correctness.rationale: Frobenius gives f³=0 in A=k[x,y]/(x³,y³). If f has nonzero linear part, local automorphism yields three Jordan 3-blocks. At quadratic leading order the degree-one-to-three map has determinant b²−ac, giving rank four or three, and f²=(b²−ac)x²y². Higher layers have ranks two, one, zero. Counting the nonzero discriminant cone over F_q gives every polynomial. Since each nonzero r-dimensional principal ideal has (q−1)q^{r−1} generators, the asserted principal-ideal counts follow. Independent q=3 rank census arithmetic gives 1,2,24,216,486,5832 by ranks and ideal counts 1,1,4,12,9,12 (39 proper; 40 total).
residual_risks: The q=3 computation is supplemental; generality depends on proof of Jordan-rank stratification and generator counts.
